hypotheses.construction_plan: Take a two-branch piecewise template parameterized by a and b: the generic branch K(a,b) applies when a != b, and the diagonal branch K(a,a) applies otherwise. Substitute a=n and b=m to produce the observed expression.
required_assumptions: K is a symbolic function of two arguments.
Ne is the two-argument inequality predicate.
proof_obligations: Piecewise((K(n, m), Ne(n, m)), (K(n, n), True)) - Piecewise((K(a, b), Ne(a, b)), (K(a, a), True))|_{a=n,b=m} = 0
hypotheses.rationale: The observed piecewise has exactly two branches whose condition is equality of the two arguments. As a parameterized object, it is the specialization of a general template with the same branch structure; the second branch is a confluent (diagonal) case of the same function K.
